nodes.name: NF cleaning
nodes.procedure: Nickel foam (NF) was tailored to 3×4 cm² and rinsed by ultrasonication in acetone, diluted hydrochloric acid, absolute ethanol, and DI water, to eliminate the oils and oxides.
nodes.source_text: Nikel foam (NF) was tailored to 3×4 cm² and rinsed by ultrasonication in acetone, diluted hydrochloric acid, absolute ethanol, and DI water

nodes.name: Hydrothermal NiMoO4·xH2O on NF
nodes.procedure: Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and (NH4)6Mo7O24 (molar ratio 4:1) dissolved in 60 mL DI water, stirred for 15 min, transferred to 100 mL Teflon-lined autoclave, hydrothermally treated at 150°C for 6 h, cooled, washed with DI water and ethanol (3x), dried at 60°C for 12 h in vacuum oven.

unit_operations.name: Solution preparation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: continuous stirring for at least 15 min

unit_operations.name: Washing and drying
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: dried in a vacuum oven at 60°C for 12 h

nodes.source_text: Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and (NH4)6Mo7O24 (molar ratio 4:1) with 60 mL of DI water... dried in a vacuum oven at 60°C for 12 h

nodes.name: NiFe-PBA ion exchange on NiMoO4
nodes.procedure: NiMoO4·xH2O immersed in 40 mL solution (20 mL solution A: 0.8 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O + C6H5Na3O7; 20 mL solution B: 0.5 mmol K3Fe(CN)6) for 26 h at room temperature to form PBA@NiMoO4.
nodes.source_text: immersed in the 40 mL aqueous solution hybrid containing 20 mL solution A (0.8 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and a certain dosage of C6H5Na3O7 and 20 ml solution B (0.5 mmol K3Fe(CN)6) for 26 h at room temperature

nodes.name: Phosphorization to Fe-Ni2P/NiMoO4
nodes.procedure: PBA@NiMoO4 and NaH2PO2·H2O placed in alumina boat (PBA@NiMoO4 downstream of Ar flow), phosphurized at 300°C for 2 h under Ar atmosphere.
nodes.source_text: NaH2PO2·H2O...put in an alumina ceramic container together with PBA@NiMoO4...phosphorization process at 300°C

nodes.name: Fe-Ni2P direct synthesis on NF
nodes.procedure: Cleaned NF immersed in 40 mL solution (0.8 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 1.2 mmol C6H5Na3O7, 0.5 mmol K3Fe(CN)6) to form NiFe-PBA, then phosphurized at 300°C for 2 h.
nodes.source_text: NF was directly immersed in the 40 mL mixed solution containing 0.8 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 1.2 mmol C6H5Na3O7 and 0.5 mmol K3Fe(CN)6...phosphorization process at 300°C

nodes.name: MoNi4 synthesis
nodes.procedure: The as-prepared NiMoO4·xH2O was heated at 400°C for 2 h in a H2/Ar (5:95) atmosphere to synthesize the MoNi4 catalyst for HER.
nodes.source_text: The as-prepared NiMoO4·xH2O was heated at 400°C for 2 h in a H2/Ar (5:95) atmosphere

nodes.name: Pt/C and RuO2 ink preparation
nodes.procedure: 20 mg commercial Pt/C or RuO2 powder was dispersed in a 2 mL mixture solution composed of 1.45 mL absolute ethanol, 0.5 mL isopropanol, and 0.05 mL Nafion solution. The homogeneous ink was obtained under ultrasonication for 2 h, and dropped upon two clean NF, respectively. Then, the Pt/C and RuO2 catalysts loading on NF were prepared after drying in a vacuum oven at 60°C for 12 h.
nodes.source_text: 20 mg commercial Pt/C or RuO2 powder was dispersed in a 2 mL mixture solution... drying in a vacuum oven at 60°C for 12 h

nodes.description: OER performance in 1 M KOH (alkaline freshwater)
nodes.source_text: We assembled a typical three-electrode system... in O₂-saturated 1 M KOH. The activated Fe-Ni₂P/NiMoO₄ catalyst exhibits the optimal OER performance... delivering current densities of 10, 100, 500, and 1000 mA cm⁻² at 197, 221, 251, and 275 mV, respectively... Fe-Ni₂P/NiMoO₄ exerts the lowest Tafel slope (30.51 mV dec⁻¹)... optimal charge transfer resistance (R_ct) of 0.77 Ω... notable long-term durability at 1.0 A cm⁻² for 1000 h in alkaline freshwater with negligible attenuation.

nodes.description: OER performance in natural alkaline seawater (1 M KOH + seawater)
nodes.source_text: we measured the OER efficiency of catalysts in... 1 M KOH + seawater solution. In Fig. 3c, d... Fe-Ni₂P/NiMoO₄ exhibits low overpotentials of 296 and 299 mV at 1000 mA cm⁻² current density in alkaline artificial and natural seawater, respectively, accompanied by low Tafel slopes (36.14 and 39.64 mV dec⁻¹)... The absence of ClER leads to a commendable Faraday efficiency of 98.41±0.67% in alkaline seawater... stable seawater electrolysis for 500 h.

nodes.description: OWS performance in alkaline seawater (AEM electrolyzer)
nodes.source_text: The MoNi₄ || Fe-Ni₂P/NiMoO₄ AEM system... achieving a cell voltage of 2.182 V at 1.0 A cm⁻²... maintained stable seawater electrolysis for 500 h at the ampere-level current density.

nodes.description: OER performance in alkaline brackish water (1 M KOH + 0.5 M NaCl)
nodes.source_text: Fe-Ni₂P/NiMoO₄ exhibits low overpotentials of 296 and 299 mV at 1000 mA cm⁻² current density in alkaline artificial and natural seawater, respectively, accompanied by low Tafel slopes (36.14 and 39.64 mV dec⁻¹).

The MoNi₄ || Fe-Ni₂P/NiMoO₄ electrode-pair can reduce the cell voltages to 1.784 and 1.798 V in alkaline freshwater and seawater... at 1.0 A cm⁻²... after 100 h of continuous freshwater/seawater splitting at ampere-scale constant current density, the system exhibits slight performance degradation.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe-Ni₂P/NiMoO₄ shows characteristic peaks of NiMoO₄·xH₂O (PDF#024-7435) and Ni₂P (PDF#074-1385) at 41.1°, 43.5°, 47.7°, 53.7° with no angle shift indicating substitutional Fe doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the characteristic peaks ascribing to N i M o O 4 ⋅ × H 2 O (PDF#024-7435) constantly persist ... new peaks emerge at 41.1, 43.5, 47.7, and 53.7° that can be indexed to N i 2 P (PDF#074-1385) ... Due to the absence of angle shift, Fe atoms are present in the N i 2 P lattice as substitutional dopants

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe-Ni₂P/NiMoO₄ shows array and top-hollow configuration retained with PBA nanocubes melted to form continuous shell layer of 900–950 nm dimensions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the array and top-hollow configuration are retained ... with dimensions ranging around 900–950 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Hierarchical nanorod structure with HRTEM showing 0.214 nm interplanar spacing indexed to (111) facet of Ni₂P.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM image obtained from the exposed interior ... interplanar parameter of 0.214 nm, which can be indexed to the (111) facet for N i 2 P.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cross-section shows hierarchical configuration with amorphous layer, Fe-Ni₂P nanoparticles, NiMoO₄·xH₂O core; lattices of 0.284 nm (02-1) and 0.306 nm (20-1) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Two labeled crystal lattices with measured interplanar distances of 0.284 and 0.306 nm are identified, which correspond to the (02-1) and (20-1) planes

nodes.characterization_summary: Magnified image confirms high crystallinity of NiMoO₄·xH₂O core with measured angle between [02-1] and [20-1] orientations aligning with theoretical 91°.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the theoretical angle between the [02-1] and [20-1] crystal orientations is calculated to be 91°, which aligns well with the measured value

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo element exclusive to core region, Fe and P predominantly on shell; larger Ni mapping area than Mo demonstrates tight binding between phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the larger mapping area of the Ni element (compared to Mo element) ... demonstrates the tight binding between Fe-Ni2P and N i M o O 4 ⋅ × H 2 ⋅ 0

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe content 7.96 at.% and Ni 34.97 at.% in Fe-Ni₂P/NiMoO₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the contents of Fe and Ni in F e - N i 2 P / N i M o O 4 is 7.96 and 34.97 at.%, respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p peaks at 856.2 and 874.0 eV for Ni²⁺ show negative shift vs pure Fe-Ni₂P and positive shift vs pristine NiMoO₄; Fe 2p shows Fe²⁺ and Fe³⁺ with positive shift for Fe³⁺ indicating higher oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the deconvoluted peaks at 856.2 and 874.0 eV corresponding to N i 2 + species exhibit a negative shift ... the significant positive shift in the bonding energy of the F e 3 + peaks

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ Raman of Fe-Ni₂P/NiMoO₄ shows Mo-O/Mo=O peaks at 347, 825, 875, 950 cm⁻¹ disappearing and γ-NiOOH peaks at 472 cm⁻¹ (E_g) and 552 cm⁻¹ (A_{1g}) appearing at lower potential of 1.40 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: characteristic bonds of Mo-O and Mo=O vibrations at 347, 825, 875, and 950 cm^{-1} gradually diminish ... γ-NiOOH can be confirmed by the presence of two characteristic peaks at 472 and 552 cm^{-1} corresponding to E_g and A_{1g} ... conversion of F e - N i 2 P / N i M o O 4 to γ-NiOOH occurs at a lower potential (1.40 V)

nodes.characterization_summary: Reconstructed R-Fe-Ni₂P/NiMoO₄ shows NiMoO₄ peaks completely disappeared, replaced by NiOOH (101) at 35.0° and (310) at 61.1° (PDF#027-0956) with residual weak Ni₂P peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: characteristic peaks of N i M o O 4 ⋅ × H 2 0 completely disappear, being replaced by two new peaks located at 35.0 and 61.1°, which can be indexed to the (101) and (310) facets of NiOOH (PDF#027-0956) ... three weak peaks located at 41.1, 47.8, and 54.6° ... attributed to residual N i 2 P species

nodes.characterization_summary: R-Fe-Ni₂P/NiMoO₄ preserves nanorod arrays morphology but evolves to loose porous structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the morphology of nanorod arrays is preserved ... individual nanorods have evolved into a loose and porous structure

nodes.characterization_summary: R-Fe-Ni₂P/NiMoO₄ shows 0.249 nm interplanar distance for (101) γ-NiOOH facet; discontinuous lattice fringes indicate Oᵥ defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the interplanar distance of 0.249 nm corresponds to the (101) facet of γ-NiOOH ... discontinuous lattice fringes are present ... ascribing to the defects via the incorporation of O V

nodes.characterization_summary: R-Fe-Ni₂P/NiMoO₄ shows uniform Fe distribution throughout nanorod; decreased Mo and P intensities from leaching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: uniform distribution of the Fe element throughout the entire nanorod ... marked decrease in the mapping intensity of Mo and P elements

nodes.characterization_summary: R-Fe-Ni₂P/NiMoO₄ shows Fe content increased to 13.32 at.% with massive Mo and P dissolution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the content of Fe is determined to be 13.32 at.% as the modifier, along with the massive dissolution of Mo and P elements

nodes.characterization_summary: R-Fe-Ni₂P/NiMoO₄ shows increased Ni³⁺/Fe³⁺ proportions, disappeared Mo/Ni-P signals, O 1s oxygen vacancy proportion increased from 28.08% to 30.98%, Ni 2p peaks positioned between R-Fe-Ni₂P and R-NiMoO₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the proportion of N i 3 + and F e 3 + of R- F e - N i 2 P / N i M o O 4 exhibits a notable increase ... XPS signals related to the Mo element and Ni-P bond almost disappear ... proportion of o v in the O 1s spectrum slightly increases from 28.08% to 30.98% ... signal peaks of Ni 2p3/2 orbital for R- F e - N i 2 P / N i M o O 4 are centered between those of R-Fe-Ni2P and R-NiMoO4

nodes.characterization_summary: Appropriate increase in Oᵥ detected in R-Fe-Ni₂P/NiMoO₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EPR spectra ... provide evidence of the appropriate increase in o v

nodes.characterization_summary: R-Fe-Ni₂P/NiMoO₄ shows I_B/I_S ratio of 1.37 vs 2.16 for R-NiMoO₄ indicating lower crystallinity from Fe migration into NiOOH lattice.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the I_B/I_S value for R F e - N i 2 P / N i M o O 4 is measured at 1.37, which contrasts sharply with the 2.16 value found in R - N i M o O 4, indicating that Fe species ... migrate into the lattice of restructured NiOOH
